rules.title: Prohibition on sale or use of coordinated pricing algorithms to set rents or manage occupancy (BMC ch. 13.63)
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to sell, license or otherwise provide to Berkeley landlords a coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in Berkeley. It is also unlawful for a landlord to use such an algorithm when setting rents or occupancy levels. A coordinated pricing algorithm uses non-public Competitor Data less than 90 days old to recommend rents, fees, occupancy rates or other lease terms in coordination between a Berkeley landlord and its competitors, including through a third-party vendor. The City Attorney and aggrieved tenants may sue. Each month of violation and each unit is a separate violation.
rules.key_value: Civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation; each month and each unit is a separate violation; damages, injunctive relief and restitution of illegal profits (City Attorney); money damages and injunctive relief (tenant); mandatory attorney's fees to the prevailing City Attorney or tenant; Competitor Data is data less than 90 days old

coverage.summary: Applies to all residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley and to landlords and vendors who sell, license or provide coordinated pricing algorithms to Berkeley landlords. No unit-count or building-age limits are stated.
coverage.other_conditions: Excluded products: (a) aggregated, anonymous rental data reports that make no rent recommendations; (b) tools for setting affordable-housing rent or income limits; (c) market research for project financing, appraisals, and research, testing or training for software development, provided Competitor Data is not an input when a recommendation is calculated.

rules.exemptions: The definition of coordinated pricing algorithm excludes aggregated and anonymous rental data reports that make no recommendations, products that set affordable-housing rent or income limits, and products used for financing market research, appraisals, or software research, testing or training.
rules.effective_date_note: The ordinance text states no effective date and no adoption date. It records only that the ordinance was passed to print and ordered published at the Council meeting of November 18, 2025.
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful for a landlord to use a coordinated pricing algorithm described in subsection A when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley.
rules.review_note: This document does not state an effective date or a final adoption date, so effective_date is left null. In_force status is inferred from the query date and the later adoption implied by the document, not stated in the text. Other sources may give a March 2026 or January 2026 effective date, but this document does not.
rules.source_notes: Official ordinance text amending BMC ch. 13.63. Council vote on November 18, 2025: 8 ayes, 0 noes, 1 absent.

result.doc_summary: Berkeley Ordinance No. 7,992-N.S. amends Berkeley Municipal Code ch. 13.63 to ban the sale, licensing and use of coordinated pricing algorithms that use non-public competitor data to set rents or occupancy levels for residential units. The ordinance defines the covered software and its exclusions, sets civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation with enforcement by the City Attorney or aggrieved tenants, and includes severability and general-welfare clauses. The text states no effective date. It records only that the ordinance was passed to print on November 18, 2025.
